warmup.text: Chapter 25 is called A Day of Death, but read closely: by the end of the chapter, who has actually died? Today's poem is a sonnet about a statue that speaks. Notice how its shape fits its voice.

words.text: Today, decide whether each word carries voc and voke, calling out, or dict, saying and declaring. Then sort words by the rule that explains their spelling. Then three new lines to finish in the game.

reading.text: Read Chapter 25 in your book. After each big moment, say in one sentence what changed. Then write your own summary sentence in the Read Like a Writer box, and finish with the Virtue Watch.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 25. Then write the first full draft of your final piece. Use what you have learned this year: strong verbs, clear pronouns, and sentences that show how ideas connect.

hook.q: Your leader just hurt one of your own. Do you keep following him?

options.reply: Many people feel that way, especially when they are afraid. Watch what the soldiers in Chapter 25 start to wonder:

options.t: I would stay, but I would be scared.
options.reply: That is just what Tingle shows in Chapter 25:

reveal.line: Privately they wondered, What might he do to me?
reveal.then: As you read Chapter 25, watch how the soldiers' fear changes into something else.

glossary.meaning: the noun a pronoun points back to
a poem of fourteen lines with a set rhyme pattern

miss.council: council (a group that meets) sounds like counsel (advice). Check the meaning.
miss.interrupt: inter + rupt. The prefix stays whole, so there are two r's.
miss.it's: it's means it is. its means belonging to it.
miss.submerge: sub + merge. The prefix stays whole.
miss.their: their means belonging to them. there and they're sound the same.
miss.transport: trans + port. The prefix stays whole.

game.title: Raise Your Voice
game.sub: This week's word game · 3 lines today
game.look: Each line is something a person in Isaac's time could say. These lines are made up; they are not from the book. Read the whole line, then tap the word that fits the blank. Each line you finish sends a gold voice ring into the sky.

do: Read the whole line, blank and all.
Ask: voice and calling, or saying?
Tap the word that fits.
Tap Next line.
how.why: If you know voc, voke and dict, you can work out words you have never studied.

game.doneLine: Come back tomorrow for three more lines.

lines.why: dict (say) + ion: the way you say your words.

lines.before: Building wagons is not just a job to me. It is my
lines.why: voc (call) + ation: work you feel called to do.

lines.after: the memory of those who came before us.
lines.why: in (on) + voke (call): to call on someone or something for help.

art.title: Oak Tree in the Snow
art.alt: A painting of a huge old oak tree in a snowy field under a gray sky, with a broken branch lying on the ground.
art.look: Caspar David Friedrich painted this old oak in the snow in Germany in 1827. Look at the broken branch on the ground. In Chapter 25, the soldiers fire into the treetops, and ice-covered branches crash down on the Choctaw Council's camp.
